The keep-out is free of copper on all four layers in both the board file and the Gerbers that will be ordered, and the moved and re-routed copper is connected and passes all rules. The board has 4.5 mm of clearance beyond the open end where Espressif asks for 15 mm. That shortfall is known and accepted for rev B, and the planned range test at bring-up covers it.

verdicts.reasoning: The geometry holds, and it is a wording nit, not a defect. I rendered datasheet v1.8 Fig. 11 (p.42) at 600 dpi, which gives 54.5 px/mm. The feed and short legs are on the pin-1 side (top-view left). Fig. 3 and the footprint put that side at device -Y. The open-end bar is the right-hand vertical bar. It sits 0.42 to 0.92 mm inside the module's +Y edge, which is device y -23.12 to -23.62, and runs from x 26.89 down to a free tip at about x 22.39 (the reviewer read 22.47). The bottom view is mirrored the same way, so the open end is at +Y and the extension is on the correct end. My pcbnew dump of the ordered board (sha256 958136...baca) shows the first copper in the antenna column (x 21.82 to 27.2) at y -18.2 on L1, L2, L3 and L4. That is 4.50 mm beyond the module edge. In the HEAD board it is 0.90 mm. One refinement: the nearest base-board copper to the tip is 0.59 mm away, at (21.80, -23.37), directly beside the tip on all four layers. On L1, L2 and L4 that copper is the GND under the module body, and on L3 it is the old VBUS track at x 21.4 to 21.8. Neither changed. The module's own ground starts at the same x 21.8 line, and Espressif wants base-board ground under the body. So the reviewer's 0.93 mm to the corner (21.8, -22.7) is a subset of a design-inherent fact. Changing the README to say 'in the antenna's own column' is optional.

findings.title: The new J1 slot geometry puts the hole edges below JLC's PTH hole-to-copper figures on L3 and L4, and the annular ring is now at JLC's 0.15 mm minimum
findings.evidence: Measured on a copy of the board (my script: scratchpad/review-a1/USBC/tools/j1check.py), comparing the new board with HEAD. (1) J1 pad 1 at KiCad (154.33, 113.76) has a 0.6 x 1.7 slot. Its end is now 0.282 mm from the In2 (L3) VBUS track, which runs from (153.18, 112.428) to (155.10, 112.428) and is 0.4 mm wide. With the old 0.8 x 1.5 slot the distance was 0.382 mm. JLC's inner-layer rule for a PTH pad hole to copper is 0.3 mm: review L13 quotes it, and the morning review confirmed it on jlcpcb.com. (2) J1 pads 1 and 4 on B.Cu: the slot hole is 0.277 mm from the ELECTRODE_5 fill (0.127 mm zone clearance plus the 0.15 mm ring). It was 0.328 mm. This morning's layout check used 0.28 mm for outer layers. (3) The annular ring is (0.9-0.6)/2 = 0.15 mm across and (2.0-1.7)/2 or (1.7-1.4)/2 = 0.15 mm at the ends. That is JLC's minimum (0.20 recommended, review L13). The old ring was 0.20 mm. KiCad DRC passes only because the board-wide hole_clearance rule is 0.2 mm, which is the via value. Every other J1 slot-to-other-net distance is 0.36 mm or more on F.Cu and 0.30 mm or more on the inner layers.
findings.fix: Before ordering, give J1 pads 1-4 a local clearance of 0.18 mm (pad property). ELE5 then refills with the hole about 0.33 mm away. Move the L3 VBUS segment at y 112.428 by 0.02 mm or more away from the slot (for example to y 112.40). Better still, add a .kicad_dru rule with hole_clearance min 0.3 mm for J1's plated pads, then refill and rerun DRC. If you change nothing, expect a JLC DFM comment on the slot clearances. ORDER.md item 2 does not list one.

findings.title: The J2 FH35C paste openings do not follow Hirose's stencil, but README Decision 12 and ORDER.md say they do: the contact-1 row is 0.70 long instead of 0.65, and every opening is centred on its pad instead of aligned to the pad's outer edge
findings.evidence: Hirose EDC3-338903-01 sheet 1, 'Recommended stencil pattern (t=0.1)'. I rendered it at 600 dpi and measured 237.5 px/mm from the 0.6 pitch. Contact-2 row openings are 0.55 +-0.02 long. The gap between the rows is 2.4 +-0.02. Contact-1 row openings are 0.65 +-0.02 long (measured 0.644 mm). The three add up to 3.6. Both rows' openings share the pad's outer edge, so the paste is pulled back from the inner side. The '0.7 +-0.02' in that drawing is the fitting opening (0.7 x 0.3, located 0.2 and 0.9 from the outer edges), not the contact-1 length. The morning verifier and the fixing agent both misread it. Gerber F_Paste as built (J2 at rot 270): pins 1,3..15 are D22 R0.700x0.230 centred at x 152.47, spanning 152.12-152.82. Hirose's opening spans 152.07-152.72, so the paste reaches 0.10 mm further toward the inner side and the contact bend. Pins 2..14 are D23 R0.559x0.230 at x 155.35, spanning 155.07-155.63, against Hirose's 155.125-155.675 (0.055 mm further inward). The paste gap between the rows is 2.25 mm against 2.40 +-0.02. The fittings (D24 0.70 x 0.30) are centred on the 0.4 x 0.95 pads, about 0.125 mm and 0.05 mm away from Hirose's edge-aligned position. The width, which drove FP-3's bridge risk, is right at 0.23. Contact-1 aperture area is 0.161 mm2 against Hirose's 0.150 (+8 percent). Wrong statements: README Decision 12 ('reproduces Hirose's openings (0.23 x 0.70 and 0.23 x 0.56)') and ORDER.md Stencil paragraph ('0.23 wide, 0.70 / 0.56 long').
findings.fix: In make_lib.py fix_land_pattern, take F.Paste off J2 pads 1-17 and add paste-only SMD rect pads (layer F.Paste only) at Hirose's positions. Contact-1 row: 0.23 x 0.65, centre 0.075 mm toward the pad's outer edge (board -x). Contact-2 row: 0.23 x 0.55, centre 0.05 mm toward the outer edge (board +x). Fittings: 0.30 x 0.70, aligned to the fitting pad's outer corner. Rebuild the paste Gerber and correct Decision 12 and ORDER.md. At bring-up, look for solder beads between J1 pad 4 and U8, and measure USB_DN (U8 pin 6) to GND before the first plug-in. If you want full fills, ask JLC in the remark to hand-touch the legs from the bottom.

findings.title: U2 exposed-pad paste is 64 percent as claimed, but the 2.0 x 2.0 opening prints straight over all four open in-pad GND vias
findings.evidence: Gerber F_Paste has R2.000x2.000 at (138.1, -115.6). U2 pad 25 is 2.5 x 2.5 at KiCad (138.1, 115.6) with solder_paste_margin -0.25. The GND vias (0.5 land, 0.3 drill) sit at (137.5/138.7, 115.0/116.2). Their lands reach 0.35-0.85 mm from the centre, all inside the +-1.0 opening. JLC cannot ink-plug vias in a pad opening (review L3/FP-7), so these are open on top and mask-tented on L4. The four barrels (about 4 x 0.057 = 0.23 mm3) can take about as much solder as the opening prints (4.0 mm2 x 0.12 x 0.51 = 0.24 mm3, or 0.20 at 0.10 mm). Expect voids or a thin EP joint. The WCH datasheet (C2858418.txt line 59) calls the EP GND 'optional but recommended', so this cannot stop the CH9102F working.
findings.fix: Optional: accept it as is. Or change the EP paste to openings that keep off the via lands (for example a cross of five squares of about 0.5 x 0.5). Or order Epoxy Filled & Capped. At bring-up, check that U2 sits flat and that all 24 pins are wetted.

- B.Cu ELE5 zone to pads 1 and 4: 0.2775 (HEAD 0.3275).

Corrections:
- The 0.15 ring is exactly HRO's own recommended 0.90 pad / 0.60 slot. Neither the review .md nor the .json has any annular-ring figure, so 'JLC minimum, 0.20 recommended, review L13' is unsupported.
- The '0.28 mm outer' figure is also not traceable in the files.
- The fixing agent accepted the same kind of case (E1 holes 0.277 from inner copper, L13) as 'at most a DFM note'.

So the likely outcome is a DFM query or a small JLC adjustment, not a failed board. Minor, because the fix is a 0.02 mm nudge of one L3 segment, or a local pad clearance.

review.area: Q4 peripheral-power switch (AO3401A, R13/R14/R34/C18/C26, GPIO13) plus the value swaps R30, C11, R9, R25
review.verdict: Ready to order. I found no blocker, major or minor problem in the Q4 change or the four value swaps. The schematic, netlist, PCB, BOM, CPL and Gerbers agree, and my own simulation supports the off-at-reset, ramp, inrush and 3V3-dip claims within a few percent. Two documented firmware constants still have their old values (Q4-1), and both must change before the first rev-A board runs firmware.

findings.title: Firmware still has the old ramp and VBUS-divider constants, and both are wrong for this board
findings.evidence: firmware/mark-8/components/slab_board/include/slab_power_seq.h:27 SLAB_PERIPH_RAMP_MS 5 (comment: 'R14 10k, C18 100 nF, about 1 ms'). slab_pins.h:40 SLAB_VBUS_DIVIDER_X1000 1667 ('100k / 150k'). With R30 at 75k, a 5.0 V VBUS puts 2.143 V on GPIO36. The firmware then computes 2143 x 1.667 = 3572 mV, which is below SLAB_VBUS_PRESENT_MV 4300, so USB is never seen as present. With the new gate network my 288-corner sweep puts 3V3_PERIPH at 0.5 V only 2.1 to 8.9 ms after GPIO13 goes low (4.3 ms for a typical part). slab_periph_on() drives SD_CS high after 5 ms, which is usually into a card with no power. tests/test_power.c:143 also asserts the old divider (5001). README 'Firmware changes this revision needs' items 1 and 2 list both changes, but they are not made yet.
findings.fix: Before you flash any firmware (slab-bringup included) on a rev-A board, set SLAB_PERIPH_RAMP_MS to 20 (my worst t90 is 12.7 ms on a cold, high-Vth part, so 20 ms leaves margin) and SLAB_VBUS_DIVIDER_X1000 to 2333. Fix the header comment and test_power.c.

findings.title: The Q4 off-state margin at reset depends on the ESP32 pull-down, which the datasheet gives only as 45k typical
findings.evidence: With 3V3 at +-2 % and R13/R14 at 1 %, VSG after reset release is 0.090 V at 80k, 0.155 V at 45k and 0.225 V at 30k. That holds Q4 off: my EKV model gives 0.23 uA at 25 C for a part at the -0.5 V minimum threshold. A hot part (Vth 0.425 V at 55 C) leaks 2.5 uA and one at 85 C (Vth 0.35 V) leaks 18 uA. If the real pull-down is stronger than assumed, VSG is 0.32 V at 20k (2.7 uA at 25 C) and 0.41 V at 15k (26 uA). At 15k and 85 C my sim lets 3V3_PERIPH float to about 1.0 V in download mode. esp32_datasheet_en.txt line 3107: RPD 45 kOhm typ, no min or max.
findings.fix: No change for rev A. On the first board, hold it in download mode and measure 3V3 minus PERIPH_GATE (expect 0.25 V or less) and 3V3_PERIPH (expect under 0.1 V).

findings.title: Q4 now runs at VGS -2.2 V, below the lowest RDS(on) test point in the datasheet
findings.evidence: With GPIO13 low, the divider gives VG = 3.3 x 1.03/3.23 = 1.05 V, so VSG = 2.22 to 2.24 V (sim). At 3V3 = 3.0 V it is 2.04 V. AO3401A (C15127 p.2) specifies RDS(on) at -10, -4.5 and -2.5 V only (85 mOhm max at -2.5 V). Fig. 5 rises steeply below -2.5 V. The old network drove the gate to 0 V (VGS -3.3 V). A square-law fit to Fig. 1 (K about 5 A/V2) gives about 0.05 to 0.2 Ohm for a max-Vth part. That is at most about 40 mV of drop at a 200 mA card peak, which is harmless.
findings.fix: No change for rev A. At bring-up, measure the drop from 3V3 to 3V3_PERIPH during an SD write burst (expect under 50 mV).

findings.title: Some numbers in q4_gate_sim.py and the README are slightly off (conclusions still hold)
findings.evidence: q4_gate_sim.py sets C_LDO = 5.0e-6 with the comment 'C11 10 uF 0603 at U4 (about 5 uF effective)'. The board's C11 is 4.7 uF 0402 CL05A475MP5NRNC, about 1.3 to 2.2 uF at 3.3 V. My re-simulation with 1.3 uF reaches the same result: the LDO peaks at 421 mA, below the 610 mA minimum limit. README Power says 'VGS stays above -0.3 V' while 3V3 powers up. With C18 at -15 % and C26 at +10 %, my sim reaches -0.372 V. That is still below the 0.5 V minimum threshold, and the rail stays at 0.036 V or less at 25 C. README says '3V3 at U1 never falls below 3.22 V', but that is only the static drop at a 3.300 V set point. With the RT9080 at -2 % it is 3.156 V. At VSYS 3.45 V (0.88 Ohm dropout) the static level is 3.086 V and the turn-on dips it to 3.031 V. The turn-on itself costs 10 mV or less (55 mV or less in dropout). README firmware change 3 says Q4 turns off 'a few milliseconds after reset release'. My sim gives 5.8 to 21.4 ms after a reset pulse.
findings.fix: Correct the C_LDO value and comment. In the README, give power-up VSG as up to -0.37 V. Say the 3.22 V figure assumes a nominal set point and a full battery. Change the turn-off-after-reset delay to 'up to about 20 ms'.

findings.title: VBUS_SENSE has no ADC filter capacitor (this was already true before the R30 change)
findings.evidence: In the netlist, /VBUS_SENSE connects only R29 pin 2, R30 pin 1 and U1 pin 4 (I36). VBAT_SENSE has C24 100 nF. Espressif HDG section 1.3.11: 'Please add a 0.1 uF filter capacitor between ESP pins and ground when using the ADC function'. The source impedance is now 100k||75k = 42.9 kOhm (it was 60 kOhm), so the change makes this better, not worse. Pin voltage: 2.14 V at 5.0 V, 2.25 V at 5.25 V, 2.36 V at 5.5 V, all below the 2.45 V calibrated limit and the 3.6 V pin limit.
findings.fix: Rev A: average several ADC samples in firmware. Rev B: add 100 nF 0402 from GPIO36 to GND.

checked: Netlist re-derived from netlist.xml and from a fresh kicad-cli export of the .kicad_sch (identical, ERC 0). Q4 pin 1 G = PERIPH_GATE, pin 2 S = 3V3, pin 3 D = 3V3_PERIPH. R13 2.2k pin 1 3V3, pin 2 PERIPH_DIV. R14 1k pin 1 PERIPH_EN_N (U1 pin 20 IO13), pin 2 PERIPH_DIV. R34 4.7k pin 1 PERIPH_DIV, pin 2 PERIPH_GATE. C18 1 uF pin 1 PERIPH_GATE, pin 2 3V3 (gate-source). C26 100 nF pin 1 PERIPH_GATE, pin 2 3V3_PERIPH (gate-drain). The PCB pad nets match all of these.

3V3_PERIPH load from the netlist and BOM: C19 and C21 10 uF 0603 CL10A106KP8NNNC, C20 and C22 100 nF, J2 VCC/IOVCC, J3 VDD, and pull-ups R21 to R24. That is 20.2 uF nominal; I modelled it with 50 % DC-bias derating at 3.3 V plus 0 to 10 uF for the screen and card.

My own DAE simulation (review-a1/Q4/sim/q4_review_sim.py; turn_on_sweep.json; more.json), 288 turn-on corners. 3V3_PERIPH reaches 90 % 2.84 to 11.1 ms after GPIO13 goes low (12.7 ms on a cold Vth 1.4 V part), with a 10-90 % rise of 0.82 to 3.69 ms. The SD-spec ramp from 0.5 V to 2.7 V takes 0.66 to 3.77 ms, inside the 0.1 to 35 ms window (SD Physical Layer v3.01 6.4.1.3), and it is monotonic. Q4 peaks at 170 mA. The RT9080 peaks at 421 mA, below its 610 mA minimum limit, so it never limits. 3V3 at U1 dips 9 mV or less at VSYS 3.6 to 4.2 V.

Power-up with GPIO13 floating (EN low), 3V3 ramp from current-limited to 5 ms: VSG peaks at 0.30 V (nominal) and 0.37 V (tolerance corner). 3V3_PERIPH stays at 0.036 V or less at 25 C and 0.11 V or less at 85 C. During reset, R13 plus R34 hold VSG at 0.

Turn-off: Q4 conducts under 10 uA 4.0 to 14.0 ms after GPIO13 goes high. VSG does not rebound, so C26 causes no glitch, and 3V3 is undisturbed. The rail falls below 0.5 V in 4 to 15 ms with a 20 to 100 mA load, or 70 to 111 ms with only the SD pull-ups (lines driven low) or a 2 mA card. Nothing actively discharges it. In deep sleep GPIO13 is RTC-held high (slab_board_prepare_deep_sleep), so VSG = 0 and R13/R14 draw no current.

GPIO13 drive: 1.03 mA steady and 1.30 mA peak while low, 0.26 mA peak while switching high. The pin stays at 0.030 to 0.039 V when low and 3.22 to 3.23 V when high. Through C26 the pin sees about 3 % of a 3V3_PERIPH transient, and nothing outside 0 to 3V3 in normal operation. Only on total power loss with Q4 on does C18 pull the gate to -2.2 V, putting the unpowered pin near its ESD clamp at sub-mA. The old network did the same.

GPIO13 (MTCK) is not a strapping pin. Reset state per the reviewer's datasheet citations: no pull during reset, wpd after release. Wake from deep sleep: release_holds() is followed at once by driving GPIO13 high, and the 6 ms gate RC rides through the gap.

Placement: R34 at (163.85, 94.3) and C26 at (164.36, 95.7, 270 deg) on F.Cu use the standard Harmony8 0402 footprints (only UUIDs changed versus HEAD). The courtyards do not overlap (R34-C26 gap 0.02 mm, R13-R34 0.09 mm, C26-D1 about 0.03 mm). R34 pad 2 and C26 pad 1 are 0.32 mm apart on the same net. kicad-cli DRC on a copy: 0 copper errors, 0 unconnected, only silkscreen warnings outside this area, no dangling tracks. PERIPH_DIV and PERIPH_GATE are 0.25 mm F.Cu only. The C26 drain via at (163.6, 96.4) lands on the existing 3V3_PERIPH L3 run, is tented in F_Mask and is present in the PTH drill file. It opens a 0.377 mm-radius hole in ELECTRODE_7 like the 7 earlier 3V3_PERIPH vias, which DISC_L3_NETS allows.

Mechanical: R34 is 0.35 mm tall in the FPC run zone (limit 4.9) and C26 is 0.5 mm in the general zone (limit 5.6), per mechanical-interface.json. Neither is near the dive or ramp zones, J3 areas A to D, the SW1 no-copper area or the antenna keep-out.

BOM/CPL/stock lines: R13 2.2k C25879 (0402WGF2201TCE), R14 1k C11702, R34 4.7k C25900, C18 1uF C52923 (CL05A105KA5NQNC), C26 100nF C1525 (CL05B104KO5NNNC X7R 16 V), C11 4.7uF C23733 (CL05A475MP5NRNC 10 V X5R), R30 75k C23242 (0603WAF7502T5E), R9 10k C25744, R25 1M C26083. All are basic parts and match the schematic values, the PCB footprint LCSC fields and the CPL (R34 and C26 rows present). The BOM has 40 lines and 84 placements, matching ORDER.md and package.json. The Gerber zip is byte-identical to gerbers/ and contains the R34/C26 pads in Cu, paste and mask.
R30 75k: VBUS x 75/175 gives 2.14 / 2.25 / 2.36 V at 5.0 / 5.25 / 5.5 V. ADC1 calibrated limit 2.45 V reached at 5.72 V. Source impedance 42.9 kOhm. The deviation is listed in README.

C11 4.7 uF 0402 X5R 10 V on 3V3 at U4 pin 5, in the same position and footprint as before. Estimated 1.3 to 2.2 uF effective at 3.3 V (tolerance -20 %, X5R), above the RT9080's 1 uF effective minimum (DS9080-05 pp.10-11). There is no upper ESR or capacitance limit, and my sim with 1.3 uF shows no current-limit event.
R9 10k: 0.5 mA and 2.8 mW at 5.25 V. On battery, D1 leakage lifts VBUS to only about 0.06 to 0.15 V, so Q3 is more fully on. VBUS_SENSE is unaffected.

R25 1M on SD_CD (GPIO15 / MTDO strap). The DM3AT detect switch is normally open with 1000 MOhm minimum insulation (100 MOhm after humidity); ESP32 IIH is 50 nA max. The high level stays at 3.2 V or more and the low level is about 0 V, against VIH 2.475 V and VIL 0.825 V. Firmware configures GPIO15 as an input with pulls off, so R25 sets the level. MPR121 coupling onto the L3 SD_CD trace is about 0.1 V, well inside the margins. The MTDO strap still sees the internal pull-up at reset.

verdicts.reasoning: Verified in the firmware tree. firmware/mark-8/components/slab_board/include/slab_power_seq.h:27 has '#define SLAB_PERIPH_RAMP_MS 5', with the comment 'R14 10k, C18 100 nF, about 1 ms'. slab_pins.h:40 has 'SLAB_VBUS_DIVIDER_X1000 1667 /* 100k / 150k */'. tests/test_power.c:143 asserts 5001. slab_power_seq.c drives SD_CS high right after the delay. slab_analog_math.c:9 returns present when vbus_mv >= 4300. With 75k: 5.0 x 75/175 = 2.143 V, and x 1.667 gives 3572 mV, below 4300, so USB is never seen as present and slab_vsys_estimate_mv falls back to VBAT. My sim puts t90 at 2.5 to 11.7 ms, so 5 ms is often too short and 20 ms is enough. README 'Firmware changes this revision needs' items 1 and 2 document both changes. This is firmware work, not a board defect, so it stays a note. It must be done before any rev-A board runs firmware.

The ESP32 datasheet (esp32_datasheet_en.txt line 3107) gives RPD 45 kOhm typical only. Line 3631 adds 'drive strength of the internal pull-up (wpu) and pull-down (wpd) is ~75 uA', which is about I_wpd x R13 = 0.165 V of VSG. My reset-release sim (sim_out_rst.json) gives the following leakage. At 25 C, min-Vth part: 0.0075 to 0.29 uA at 45k and 0.06 to 1.1 uA at 30k (n 1.3 to 2.0). At 55 C: 1.4 to 8.6 uA at 30k. At 85 C: 4 to 16 uA at 45k and 20 to 48 uA at 30k. With 15k or a 150 uA sink at 25 C: 1.6 to 34 uA. This is in line with the reviewer. Typical parts (Vth 0.9 V) are below 1 nA. Q4 is effectively off, and the old network was fully on here, so the change is strictly better. One caveat on the reviewer's bring-up fix: '3V3_PERIPH under 0.1 V in download mode' is a valid Q4 test only with the screen and card removed (see the missed item). Measuring 3V3 minus PERIPH_GATE is the robust check.

The divider gives VG = 3.3 x (1k + 30R) / (2.2k + 1k + 30R) = 1.05 V, and my sim gives on-state VSG 2.23 V (2.14 V at VSYS 3.45 V with a -2 % set point). The AO3401A (C15127 p.2) specifies RDS(on) only at -10, -4.5 and -2.5 V (85 mOhm max at -2.5 V). With Kp fitted to those points (about 12 A/V2, swept 6 to 25), a cold max-Vth part drops up to 22 mV at 100 mA in my sweep, about 0.2 ohm. At 200 mA that is about 40 mV. This is harmless, and a bring-up measurement is enough.

q4_gate_sim.py:42 has 'C_LDO = 5.0e-6  # C11 10 uF 0603 at U4', but the board's C11 is 4.7 uF 0402 C23733. The result does not change: in my sim the LDO peaks at about 415 mA (250 mA ESP32 plus 165 mA Q4), never reaching 610 mA. README 'never falls below 3.22 V' is the static drop 3.3 - 0.25 x (0.055 + 0.22) = 3.231 V, while the turn-on itself costs only 9 mV or less. With a -2 % set point and VSYS 3.45 V my sim gives 3.06 V. README 'VGS stays above -0.3 V' while powering up: my sim gives -0.285 V nominal and -0.34 V with C18 -10 % and C26 +10 %. The reviewer's -0.37 V uses C18 -15 %. README 'a few milliseconds after reset release': analytically tau is about 7 ms and VSG falls below Vth 3.5 to 17 ms later. Also, README 'Q4 stops conducting 3.5 to 10.6 ms' becomes up to about 21 ms at 85 C in my turn-off sweep. These are documentation inaccuracies only.

In the netlist, /VBUS_SENSE is only R29.2, R30.1 and U1.4 (I36), with no capacitor. /VBAT_SENSE has C24 100 nF. hdg.txt line 767: 'Please add a 0.1 uF filter capacitor between ESP pins and ground when using the ADC function'. The source impedance is now 100k || 75k = 42.9k (it was 60k), so the change improves this. Pin voltages: 2.14 / 2.25 / 2.36 V at 5.0 / 5.25 / 5.5 V, all under the 2.45 V calibrated limit, which is reached at 5.72 V. Unpowered-pin injection on a 3V3 ramp is under 40 uA (it was about 50 uA). This was already true before the change; averaging samples in firmware is enough for rev A.

missed.title: With Q4 now off at reset, the GPIO5 and GPIO14 reset pull-ups feed the unpowered microSD card and screen through their input clamps during boot and download mode. The rail is not 'off', and the bring-up check '3V3_PERIPH under 0.1 V in download mode' will fail on a good board
missed.evidence: netlist.xml: /SD_SCK = J3 pin 5 CLK and U1 pin 29 (IO5). /LCD_SCK = J2 pin 5 SCLK and U1 pin 18 (IO14). The ESP32 IO_MUX table (esp32_datasheet_en.txt line 4035, chip pin 34 GPIO5) gives 'oe=0, ie=1, wpu' at reset and after reset. Line 4006 (pin 17 MTMS = GPIO14) gives 'oe=0, ie=0' at reset and 'oe=0, ie=1, wpu' after reset. Line 3631: the wpu is about 75 uA. Before the fix, GPIO13's pull-down turned Q4 on at reset, so these pull-ups drove powered parts. Now Q4 is off from reset release until slab_board_init() runs: ROM, bootloader, the PSRAM test and app start, and indefinitely in download mode. During that time two 45k pull-ups source up to about 70 uA each into the CLK and SCLK pins of an unpowered card and screen. This is the case SD Physical Layer v3.01 section 6.4.2 warns about ('DAT, CMD, and CLK should be disconnected or driven to logical 0 ... to avoid ... operating current drawn through the signal lines'), and README firmware note 1 / SPEC 5.3 forbid it in firmware. The current is far too small to damage anything. But 3V3_PERIPH can sit at an intermediate level (roughly 1 to 2.5 V, depending on the card and the screen's low-voltage draw), so README Power bullet 2 ('Q4 stays off ... also in download mode') must not be read as 'the rail is off'. The reviewer's Q4-2 bring-up expectation for 3V3_PERIPH is also invalid unless the screen and card are removed. No hardware change for rev A: the CC-2 firmware item (wait until the GPIO25 reading of the rail is below 0.4 V before turning Q4 on) already covers the card's power-cycle requirement. At bring-up, judge Q4 by 3V3 minus PERIPH_GATE (0.25 V or less), or measure 3V3_PERIPH with J2 and J3 empty.

review.area: FAB: the JLCPCB fabrication and assembly package (frame, Gerbers, drills, CPL, BOM, ORDER.md, build guide)

verdicts.reasoning: I measured this with my own pcbnew dump of the work board (REG-verify/gW.json, j1paste.py, j1b.py), and the geometry holds. J1 pad 1 is a 0.90 x 2.00 oval at KiCad (154.33,113.76) with paste margin +0.25, so the opening is 1.40 x 2.50. F_Paste.gtp has D53 = O 1.4x2.5 flashed at X154.33 Y-113.76 and D54 = O 1.4x2.2 on pads 2 and 3. HEAD had no F.Paste on these pads. The LCD_MOSI segment (155.2548,114.4235)-(152.8766,116.8017), w 0.15, is 0.209 mm copper-to-copper from pad 1. The opening covers 0.0129 mm2 of that track. The pad 4 opening is 0.287 mm from U8.6 (USB_DN, exposed pad), and the pad 2 opening is 0.127 mm from the VBUS 0.4 mm track. One correction: LCD_MOSI is under solder mask, so paste printed over it cannot connect to it. Paste on mask pulls back to the pad when it melts. The reviewer did not list the more relevant neighbours: the pad 2 opening is 0.044 mm from the ring of the CHG_STAT via at (155.11,116.93) and 0.077 mm from the VBUS via at (153.48,116.97). Both vias are within 0.35 mm of J1 pad 2's copper, so JLC tents them instead of plugging them. If a tent fails, molten paste sits about 0.14 to 0.18 mm from an open barrel, and VBUS or CHG_STAT could short to the GND shell. Decision 11 assumes a 0.12 mm stencil, but ORDER.md line 65 asks for 0.10 mm. My estimate is about 38 to 45 percent slot fill at 0.12 and 31 to 37 percent at 0.10. The chance of a fault is low, a meter finds it before first power, and it can be reworked, so minor is right. A smaller or custom paste opening on the pad 2 side costs little.
